seo.title: Common Multiples of 3 and 5 - LCM Grid Speed Challenge
seo.metaDescription: Click all common multiples of 3 and 5 on a 100-tile grid. Practice least common multiple (LCM) and divisibility concepts under time pressure.
seo.intro: A common multiple is a shared multiple of two or more distinct integers. The least common multiple (LCM) of 3 and 5 is 15. Consequently, any number that is a common multiple of both 3 and 5 must be a multiple of 15. In this speed game, students identify numbers on the 100-grid that satisfy divisibility by both 3 and 5 simultaneously, reinforcing algebraic factors and fraction denominators.
seo.howToPlay: Find every number from 1 to 100 that is divisible by both 3 and 5. Correct clicks turn green with a checkmark icon. Incorrect selections flash red and subtract 2 seconds from the clock. Find all 6 common multiples before time expires.
seo.teacherNotes: Connect this exercise to finding least common denominators (LCD) when adding fractions with unlike denominators 1/3 and 1/5.

faq.q: What are all common multiples of 3 and 5 up to 100?
faq.a: Because the LCM of 3 and 5 is 15, the common multiples between 1 and 100 are 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, and 90.

faq.q: How can you test if a number is a multiple of both 3 and 5?
faq.a: First, check if the last digit is 0 or 5 (divisibility rule for 5). Next, add the digits together and check if their sum is divisible by 3.
